caption: Graph input: a sub-graph's speed pin - previewed on its own, at its default of 0.3
why: A piece of graph you use again and again - a fire, a sparkle layer, a scroll - can become a node of its own: a sub-graph. Graph input and Graph output are its pins: each Graph input becomes an input of the node, each Graph output an output.

Select nodes and Node > Fold into a sub-graph makes one, with these pins already in place. Its neighbours: Send and Receive carry values within one graph; Graph input and output carry them in and out of a sub-graph.
steps: **name** is speed: the pin the node made from this graph will show.
**type** is float, a number. **default** is 0.3: what it gives when nothing is wired to the pin - and what the preview runs at.
Its `value` times **Time** scrolls a **Palette**; the colour leaves by a **Graph output** named colour.
Save it in the project's subgraphs and it appears in the add menu as a node with a speed input and a colour output.

try.label: Faster default
try.text: default 1: the pin's default triples the scroll - in the preview, and wherever the node is used with speed unwired.
